title: Mixed to 100
subtitle: + − to 100, × ÷ to 15
bounds: Mixed facts (PROTOCOL 4c, briefs/facts2): the whole run inside + and − to 100 and × and ÷ with factors to 15, easy to hard by tier. Each tier is 6 items from each of facts-add-100, facts-sub-100, facts-mul-15, facts-div-15 at the same tier: the same pools, forms, distractors, explanations and student text, every part's floor n scaled to ceil(n / 4), at most 2 zero-factor multiplication prompts a tier; 24 items per tier, prompts unique per tier, operations interleaved. Misconception keys carry their operation (ADD_, SUB_, MUL_, DIV_). Answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each over the whole tier. [ADD] Facts bounds (PROTOCOL 4c, briefs/facts2): the whole run inside sums 51 to 100, easy to hard by tier. Prompt forms: R 'a + b = ?' (answer s), C 'a + ? = s' (answer b), S '? + b = s' (answer a); every number a non-negative integer. T1 R, an operand a non-zero multiple of ten. T2 R, no multiple of ten and the ones stay under ten: >= 8 with a one-digit operand, >= 8 with both two-digit. T3 the same with the ones making a ten. T4 C, a, b >= 2, no multiple of ten (>= 12 regrouping). T5 S (>= 12, >= 6 regrouping) and C (>= 6 regrouping), a, b >= 2, no multiple of ten. Prompts unique per tier, 24 per tier. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers <= 999, >= 2 near the answer (+-1, +-2, +-10), at most 1 far; answer rank among the 4 values 15-35% each per tier; answers >= 20 always have a wrong choice sharing the ones digit (+-10); the answer is never the only value of its parity. [SUB] Minuends 51-100, a and b at least 2 (T1 allows 1). T1 R with a multiple of 10 as a or b; T2 R no trade (the ones of s at least the ones of a), at least 8 with a one-digit part and 8 with both parts at least 10; T3 R with a trade, same two floors; T4 s − ? = b, at least 12 with a trade, no multiples of 10; T5 ? − a = b (at least 12, 6 with a trade) and s − ? = b (6 with a trade), no multiples of 10. Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least two within 1, 2 or 10 of the answer, at most one far; where the answer is 20 or more one wrong choice shares its ones digit; modelled misconceptions first, ARITH only to fill; each answer rank (smallest to largest of the four) holds the answer in 15-35% of a tier. [MUL] Factors 0 to 15. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: the easy rows (0, 1, 2, 5, 10) and 11 times a digit, at least 12 with a factor of 11 to 15 (147 prompts); T2 R: a factor of 11-15 times 3 or 4, not an easy fact (at least 12; 43 prompts with the 3-4-9 core); T3 R: a factor of 11-15 times 6-15, not an easy fact (at least 12), else a 6, 7 or 8 core fact (84); T4 C: hard facts with a factor of 11-15 (at least 12), else any hard fact with factors 3-15 (109); T5 S: hard facts with a factor of 11-15 (at least 8), any hard fact (at least 4), plus C (at least 4 with 11-15; 218 prompts in all). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far; with a factor of 11 or more and an answer of 20 or more, one wrong value shares the answer's ones digit. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier. [DIV] PROTOCOL 4c, facts range cartridge. Forms: R is p ÷ a = ? (answer the quotient), C is p ÷ ? = b (answer the divisor), S is ? ÷ a = b (answer the dividend); p = a × b, the times table read backwards, never ÷ 0, no 0 ÷ ? = 0. Divisors and quotients 0-15, the 11-15 rows are the point. T1 R: easy rows to 15, at least 12 with an 11-15. T2 R: 11-15 with 3 or 4 (at least 12). T3 R: 11-15 with 6-9 or 11-15 pairs (at least 12). T4 C: 3-15 facts with an 11-15 (at least 12). T5 S: 3-15 facts with an 11-15 (at least 8), any 3-15 fact (at least 4), plus C (4 with an 11-15). Wrong choices: distinct non-negative integers up to 999, at least 2 near and at most 1 far. R: near within 2 of the quotient (GROUP_OFF q+-1, +-2), far SUBTRACTED p-a, MULTIPLIED p×a, TENS_SLIP q+-10. C: near within 2 of the divisor (MISSING_ONE_OFF a+-1, ARITH +-2), far MISSING_SUBTRACTED p-b, MISSING_MULTIPLIED p×b. S: near within the larger factor of the dividend (START_GROUP_OFF p+-a, START_ADDED a+b, START_TENS p+-10 when a factor is 11 or more, with a twin ones digit when p is 20 or more). The answer's rank among the four values is spread 15-35% per tier.

tiers.name: Easy facts
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷: the easy facts from each operation.

tiers.name: Building facts
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷: the next facts from each operation.

tiers.name: Harder facts
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷: the hardest plain facts from each operation.

tiers.name: Missing numbers
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷, a number missing: 4 + ? = 9, 12 ÷ ? = 3.

tiers.name: Missing first numbers
tiers.description: A mix of + − × ÷, often the first number missing: ? − 6 = 9.

ADD_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Count again: start at the bigger number and count up.
ADD_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted on wrong: the sum is one more or one less than the true sum.

ADD_SUBTRACTED.student: Plus means put together. Add the two numbers, don't take them apart.
ADD_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracted the smaller addend from the larger instead of adding: 8 + 5 = 3.

ADD_NO_CARRY.student: The ones made a new ten. Add that ten in with the tens.
ADD_NO_CARRY.teacher: Dropped the regrouped ten when the ones summed to 10 or more: 38 + 47 = 75.

ADD_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Add the tens, then the ones.
ADD_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Tens digit of the sum is one too many or too few, with the ones right: 34 + 52 = 76 or 96.

ADD_MISSING_ADDED.student: Don't add the two numbers you see. Find the missing one: subtract.
ADD_MISSING_ADDED.teacher: Added the shown number and the total instead of subtracting: 7 + ? = 15 answered 22.

ADD_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Add your answer to the shown number and check the total.
ADD_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted up wrong: the missing number is one more or one less than the true one.

ADD_MISSING_TENS.student: Check the tens. Add your answer to the shown number: is it the total?
ADD_MISSING_TENS.teacher: Missing number is ten too many or too few: forgot the trade counting up across a ten, or a tens slip.

SUB_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Check: answer + number taken away must equal the start.
SUB_ONE_OFF.teacher: Counted back one step too many or too few: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 1.

SUB_ADDED.student: Take away, don't add. Subtracting makes the number smaller.
SUB_ADDED.teacher: Added the two numbers (s + a) instead of subtracting.

SUB_SMALLER_FROM_LARGER.student: Don't flip digits. If the top digit is smaller, trade a ten for 10 ones.
SUB_SMALLER_FROM_LARGER.teacher: In each place takes the smaller digit from the larger (14 - 6 gives 12; 52 - 38 gives 26) instead of regrouping.

SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.student: You traded a ten for ones, so the tens digit has to drop by one.
SUB_FORGOT_TRADE.teacher: Regrouped the ones but left the tens unchanged: answer is 10 too big (14 - 6 gives 18; 52 - 38 gives 24).

SUB_TENS_SLIP.student: The tens are off by one ten. Check: answer + taken away = start.
SUB_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: answer is the correct difference plus or minus 10.

SUB_MISSING_ADDED.student: Add the missing part to what is left and you must get the start. Check it.
SUB_MISSING_ADDED.teacher: s - ? = b: added the two numbers shown (s + b) instead of finding what was taken away.

SUB_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Off by one. Put your number back in the problem and check it.
SUB_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing number is one too big or too small (the answer plus or minus 1); did not check by substituting.

SUB_MISSING_TENS.student: Off by one ten. Put your number back in the problem and check it.
SUB_MISSING_TENS.teacher: Right ones, tens digit one too high or too low: the missing number plus or minus 10 (trade forgotten or tens slip).

SUB_START_SUBTRACTED.student: The start is bigger than both numbers: add back what was taken away.
SUB_START_SUBTRACTED.teacher: ? - a = b: took the two shown numbers apart (|b - a|) instead of adding back what was taken.

MUL_GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
MUL_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

MUL_ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
MUL_ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

MUL_DROPPED_CARRY.student: Keep the ten: 13 × 6 is 60 + 18, and the 18 has a ten to add in.
MUL_DROPPED_CARRY.teacher: Splits into tens and ones but loses the ten from the ones product: 13 × 6 = 60 + 8 = 68.

MUL_TENS_SLIP.student: Check the tens place. Split into tens and ones, multiply each, add both.
MUL_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Right ones digit, tens place off by one ten (product plus or minus 10).

MUL_PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.student: Tens × tens plus ones × ones skips two parts. Split one number, multiply both.
MUL_PARTIAL_PRODUCTS.teacher: Multiplies tens by tens and ones by ones only: 13 × 14 = 100 + 12 = 112.

MUL_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MUL_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MUL_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MUL_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MUL_MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MUL_MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.

DIV_GROUP_OFF.student: Close: a group or two off. Multiply your answer by the divisor to check.
DIV_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Quotient off by one or two: counted a group or two too many or too few.

DIV_SUBTRACTED.student: Divide, don't subtract. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
DIV_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend (p − a) instead of dividing.

DIV_MULTIPLIED.student: Divide, don't multiply. Ask how many of the divisor fit in the dividend.
DIV_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies dividend and divisor (p × a) instead of dividing.

DIV_TENS_SLIP.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply back to check the size.
DIV_TENS_SLIP.teacher: Quotient off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

DIV_MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: One off. Try your number in the problem: does the division work out?
DIV_MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing divisor off by one: stopped a fact early or late in the table.

DIV_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Don't subtract. Ask: what times the answer shown makes the dividend?
DIV_MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts (p − b) to find the missing divisor instead of asking what times b makes p.

DIV_MISSING_MULTIPLIED.student: Too big. Divide the dividend by your number: is it the answer shown?
DIV_MISSING_MULTIPLIED.teacher: Multiplies (p × b) to find the missing divisor instead of dividing or asking what times b makes p.

DIV_START_GROUP_OFF.student: One group off. Multiply the two numbers you see, no more, no less.
DIV_START_GROUP_OFF.teacher: Missing dividend off by one divisor (a × (b +- 1)): counted one group too many or too few.

DIV_START_ADDED.student: Don't add. To undo dividing, multiply the two numbers you see.
DIV_START_ADDED.teacher: Adds the divisor and quotient (a + b) to find the missing dividend instead of multiplying back.

DIV_START_TENS.student: Right ones digit, wrong tens. Multiply the two numbers, then check the size.
DIV_START_TENS.teacher: Missing dividend off by ten: right ones digit, tens place slipped.

items.explanation: 0 × 11 = 0: no groups, or groups of nothing, make 0. Anything times 0 is 0.
0 ÷ 1 = 0: zero shared into groups of 1 leaves none, and 1 × 0 = 0.
15 ÷ 3 = 5 because 3 × 5 = 15. Neighbour fact: 3 × 4 = 12, plus one more 3.
1 × 15 = 15: one group of 15. Any number times 1 is itself.
5 × 8 = 40: half of 8 × 10 = 80, and half of 80 is 40.
10 × 6 = 60: ten groups of 6, so put a zero after 6.
13 ÷ 13 = 1: any number divided by itself is 1.
28 ÷ 4 = 7 because 4 × 7 = 28. Neighbour fact: 4 × 6 = 24, plus one more 4.
79 − 3 = 76: the ones are 9 − 3 = 6, the tens stay.
4 + 65 = 69: the tens stay, the ones go from 5 to 9.
76 − 2 = 74: the ones are 6 − 2 = 4, the tens stay.
3 + 73 = 76: the tens stay, the ones go from 3 to 6.
62 + 4 = 66: the tens stay, the ones go from 2 to 6.
18 ÷ 3 = 6 because 3 × 6 = 18. Neighbour fact: 3 × 5 = 15, plus one more 3.
68 − 59: count up from 59 to 68, 9 steps. Check: 59 + 9 = 68.
63 − 9: take 3 to get 60, then take 6 more: 54.
73 − ? = 54: count up from 54 to 73, that is 19. So 73 − 19 = 54, ? = 19.
8 × ? = 32: 8 × 4 = 32, so ? = 4. Count by 8s up to 32, or divide: 32 ÷ 8 = 4.
196 ÷ ? = 14: 14 × 14 = 196, so ? = 14. A square fact: 14 times itself makes 196.
? − 8 = 67: undo the take away, 67 + 8 = 75, so ? = 75. Check: 75 − 8 = 67.
7 × ? = 84: 7 × 12 = 84, so ? = 12. Count by 7s up to 84, or divide: 84 ÷ 7 = 12.
